productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Touch screen intermittent; battery does not hold chargeTouch screen intermittent; battery does not hold charge
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Be mindful when purchasing USED products.While they go above and beyond in the marketing of the device “factory re-manufactured” and “certified pre-owned” and ETC are all fancy wording for SECOND HAND, and USED.That said, with high hopes I purchased this device in May 2024 for my birthday, everything seemed to work fine, even though I noticed that the Maximum Battery Capacity was below 90%. —- Now in late January 2025 roughly only 8 months of use and the MBC has fallen to 77%, which has shown extreme degradation in that it cannot hold a charge.In addition, I have noticed that the touch screen is intermittent-Meaning that sometimes it works, and sometimes it does not. Sometimes no have to press multiple times and extremely firm—Note that all softer is up to day on the iOS, as well as the Apps used.Also note that I have equipped this phone with a highend sturdy case, which has kept it well protected, although it has not suffered any falls or drops of any kind.Additionally, the screen is and has been protected and covered since the day I received the phone and it still intact with NO cracks or scratches —-All that said, aside from the disappointment of the battery not being at 99% when received and now not holding a charge through the day even with a mid day recharge, I am surprised that I could not get to at least a full 2 years before minor or even major hardware degradation had set in.The question then lies with the company who is selling the phones vs the Apple product itself.I can say ALL my Apple iPhone devices have held the test of time and I’ve never had to upgrade due to hardware, but due to obsoletion.SO, it is my assessment that the company selling the second hand item needs to do a better job checking the devices before resale, as well as fairly pricing it for its age and prior use.-not to mention changing the battery component if it is below 90%.The one, and only good thing I can say was the phone appeared relatively new with little evidence of use meaning just monor scratches on the metal chassis housing, although this goes completely unnoticed as the phone is covered completely with protection.The status of the companies integrity is still up for debate, if they can accommodate my request for a replacement to a newer iPhone model, for which I will pay the difference I will then say happy shopping to all customers, if not, I will say be WEARY of buying used, older model iPhone devices by smaller relatively unknown companies.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ll preface this review by saying I am pretty picky when it comes to my possessions.  My IPhone 7+ finally gave up the ghost.  I was hoping to get through the remainder of this year so that when the IPhone 15 came out that I would get a renewed 14 Max Pro but that was not to be.  We had purchased a renewed IPhone 12 for my son from another seller and were surprised with how clean it was when it arrived.  We paid extra for the excellent condition and it was in pristine condition with a 100% battery max battery health.Prime day comes along and I see this phone from this seller.  It was roughly $200 more than the regular IPhone 12 that we bought for my son but it was the Pro model and it did have 512k of storage.  Due to the positive experience we had with the earlier purchase, I decided to pull the trigger.Fulfillment was great.  I had ordered the phone on 7/11 and it was scheduled to arrive on 7/14 but to my surprise it hit my house on 7/13 which was a nice surprise.When I picked up the package I got worried because I could hear and feel something rattling in the box that was shipped in a form fitting padded envelope.  To my relief I found the phone  to be intact.  It arrived with protective plastic on the screen, a SIM port tool, and a lightning charging cable that was loose in the box.  Upon inspection I found the screen to be free of scratches or gouges but there is some slight surface marring on a small section of the screen that you have to look for in order to see.  The bezel was clean except for a couple of nicks.  The worst sign of usage is a chip above the top of the highest camera lens.  It’s not huge but you can definitely see it and it looks like a chip in a car windshield since the back of the phone is finished in glass.  The only other thing to mention is that there was a bit of what looks like green metal tape that was poking out of the side of the phone between the screen and bezel which I was able to rub off with my fingernail.  It looked like the refurb process was not as clean as it could have been.Going into the settings I found that the max battery life was only 85% which was kind of a bummer.  Setting up the phone was a breeze with ICloud but I haven’t figured out how to pull down the pictures that resided on my old phone.  My apps came over but know I had to re-enter my passwords in most cases.After only a couple of day usage, everything seems to work fine.  Amazon gives 90 days to return for any issues.  The camera on the pro is a definite improvement over the 7+.  Size wise the unit is smaller than the 7+ but the screen is bigger on the 12 since it doesn’t have the home button at the bottom which I keep wanting to press out of habit.Overall the purchase was better than ok.  If the phone has another 10% of battery life and the nick on the camera was not present then I would rate the item as excellent.  I’ll always wonder if I should have purchased a phone from the other seller that sold a phone in perfect condition.  I will update this review should anything major happen with the phone.

A brick!  Off to UBreakWeFix thinking I'd delayed the new battery too long.  Was STUNNED to learn it was irreparable due to- wait for it!-- water damage.  It stays on the bathroom counter when I'm listening to music in the shower.  When my husband was recovering from something last year, I did take it into the pool area at my gym, ringer on loud in case he needed me- left in my bag on a hook or bench.  At most it's gotten a drop or two on the (protected) screen, quickly wiped dry. My son's laughing at me because he researched iPhone 12 is rated to be **underwater** for 30 minutes (THAT surprised me!).  Anyway, who knows what it's 'wet' history was before me. The price beat buying new, but I've always gotten several YEARS of use...Just 14 months this time.  Buying new from source from now on.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: El Apple iPhone 12 Pro, en su versión de 128GB, es un dispositivo que no deja de impresionar en todos los aspectos. Desde su diseño hasta su rendimiento, este teléfono inteligente de Apple se destaca como una opción premium para aquellos que buscan lo mejor en tecnología móvil.Comenzando por su diseño, el iPhone 12 Pro exhibe una estética elegante y sofisticada. Su construcción de vidrio y acero inoxidable le brinda una sensación de calidad y durabilidad, mientras que los bordes planos y la pantalla OLED sin bordes le dan un aspecto moderno y atractivo. Además, cuenta con la certificación IP68, lo que significa que es resistente al agua y al polvo, brindando tranquilidad en situaciones cotidianas.La pantalla Super Retina XDR de 6.1 pulgadas es simplemente impresionante. I had the S24 Ultra and returned in the same week when it came out.My biggest gripe with S24+, and now with the entire android platform is Google. Almost every App thats in Google Play Store, is developed using Google Firebase, with Analytics. At least 80% of all apps contain Analytics. The analytics can measure what buttons you tap, how long you spend on the screen, etc. I find this deeply invasive, and hence nothing on the Android phone is private when you pair it with Google Play backend telemetry. If I go on Apple they decouple the telemetry, so its not associated with your account, Google on the otherhand does not do that. Apps on Android have a lot more room to run in the background as well.

While others are receiving the new One UI 8.0 update, my phone is completely locked out.​Outdated Security: The device claims it is "up to date," but the actual software information shows a Security patch level of November 1, 2024. This means the phone has not received a security patch in an entire year (as of late 2025) and is vulnerable.​Technical Confirmation of the Problem:​When attempting a manual software update, the system reports the following information, which confirms the update mechanism is broken:​Update information:One UI version: 6.1, Android version: 14Current version: S926USQU4AXK5 / S926UOYN4AXK5 / S926USQU4AXK5Security patch level: November 1, 2024​The retailer's response confirms this is a severe and unfixable flaw:​I contacted my carrier, Amazon, and the manufacturer (if applicable). Amazon's technical support provided a definitive, alarming response:​"FOTA is also not supported in this version. (210) The version of the device is NOT supported. (No delta for the version)"​This technical response indicates that the specific software build on this phone is not recognized by the standard update server and cannot receive the necessary "delta" (the small file needed to transition from the old version to the new one). This confirms the phone is permanently stuck on this outdated and potentially insecure version. strongly regret this purchase and cannot wait to replace this phone with a new one bought elsewhere. Please do not make the same mistake.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My son has Type 1 Diabetes and has needed a cell phone since he was diagnosed for tracking his glucose monitor and allowing us to track it. He has always used a Samsung, and he needs to have a fairly current model because the apps the monitoring companies use require certain specifications (like most current system updates). When his S20 wouldn't update anymore we upgraded to this and so far it has worked great. The only complaint I have is that the transfer from the old phone to new phone was not as smooth as other phone brands. I have transferred phone data for myself and my kids a LOT of times and every time, the apps and wallpaper and everything transfers, you don't even hardly know you have a new phone. This one only initially uploaded all the "spam" crappy apps from Samsung that you don't want or need, and with his Google account some of the Google stuff did transfer. However, I had to do a lot of toggling back and forth between his old and new phones to get the rest of his apps and data transferred and it was a pain and took way too much time! We also had to re-log in to many apps which I haven't had to do with other phone transfers so yeah. But the battery life on this is great, the camera is really nice, screen is a bit larger (not a ton) than the past models, and operating system is user friendly.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: These Amazon renewed Samsung phones are our new favorites
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It started with ordering a renewed Samsung S5E Tablet that won me over to ordering Amazon Renewed electronics. That well regarded tablet arrived without a mark on it, a charger and cable. It works perfectly and I use it almost every day. I especially like the DeX mode for some work-related tasks. Being the "thrifty" guy that I am, I set maximum price limits on many products that I buy. Phones are in that group of products. I don't think it necessary to buy the latest Flagship phones from any of the major phone brands or even many of their high-end models. When introduced the Samsung 21 FE 5G had many positive reviews with one major complaint, for its high price, considering it was supposed to be a value product.After a bad drop of a OnePlus 7T that killed the screen of my wife's phone, it was time to order two new phones [that is, new for us], one for her and one for me. I'm a tech guy and I always order two of the same phones since it's easier for me to support a single model of phone. Having used Samsung phones years ago but then moving to ZTE and the OnePlus, these S21 FE phones have been terrific after one month of use and renewed my interest in Samsung phones. The phones arrived in like new condition without any marks or scratches on either phone. Unlike the new models these both came with 20W chargers and good quality 5ft cables. These phones have a plastic case which I prefer, as plastic is less fragile than glass, which is another reason for me to NOT buy flagship phones. I am also not so concerned with the appearance or color of the phones since I immediately put them in a case and install tempered glass screen protectors on all my phones.Among the many positives are the 120HZ screen response is a pleasure to use, battery life has been excellent lasting for more than a day for normal use including text, calls, email, YouTube and some streaming, terrific camera, good stereo speakers, charges very quickly with the supplied chargers but also with the 25W aftermarket chargers that I have for these phones. Both Fingerprint and Face recognition work consistently and more quickly than other phones I have used. Bluetooth and WiFi connect quickly without any dropouts, and speed on T-Mobile 5g for phone and Home Internet has been consistent within the T-Mobile performance spec for my location. I am not a gamer so I can't provide a meaningful review for that.The only negative I can report is for the amount of Samsung bloatware and the numerous and annoying notifications, which can luckily be turned off. These are two excellent phones that I bought for less than half the price of one new one. And the Amazon renewed program is a good and safe option for many purchases as it also includes a 90-day return policy if there is any dissatisfaction with the product.

I set it down not thinking next to my iPhone 12 plus, I had no ideal anything would happen till I heard it kind of vibration , when I picked up the phone to look at it it was everything had transferred cause they were only sitting on the table while I went and did something else in the house so, when I come back, I could see the picture of my dog on the front of the new phone and I was like wow what happened if I didn’t know better I would’ve been like it’s gonna take me 45 minutes to an hour and that’s really why it took me three days to open it up, I just did not have time to deal with carrier and Technician for support, and all that drama with cloud and transferring data to one phone from the other.I just did not have the time to get on the phone with the (carrier) and go through all the Rigamarole so to speak .Let me tell you when I saw the dog picture on the new phone. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Such a beautiful designed iPhone 16 Pro Max
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Ok, I’m a galaxy gal with a S25 Ultra phone.  People tell me try Apple’s iPhone, and I put it off for more than 12 years.  However, I do own 2 Apple Mac Minis, and I like the computers.  Well, I looked up iPhones on Amazon and other sites and came across this iPhone 16 Max Pro with 8 gig ram and 1 terabyte storage for just a little over 900 dollars.  A lot of money for an iPhone that’s a year old I thought.So I took the risk and made the purchase.When I got the package in the mail I hesitated even opening the box and contemplated just returning it back without giving it a chance.  Well, after opening the box and charging it up, I transferred my data over to the iPhone 16 Pro Max and it worked well and fairly easy too.I still wasn’t too impressed with the iPhone just yet, but I gave it a chance.As I began using it and saw the battery life was at 98 % I thought, WOW, nice iPhone with a pretty decent battery too.  I also noticed it still has an Apple warranty until March of 2026.The phone is beautiful and works great thus far, but my niece said I should get the iPhone 17 Pro Max.  So I looked it up and didn’t see why I should go into a 2k debt for an iPhone 17 pro max with a 1 terabyte storage drive.  After all, my iPhone 16 Pro Max still gets another 6 years of updates on the iOS software.I have to say I still have time to return this iPhone, but, right now, this is a well made and solid purchase and I feel very comfortable with it after 2 weeks of use.  I still have my android Galaxy S25 Ultra, and I’m gonna keep it too, but the seller of this iPhone certainly does ship out beautiful and quality iPhones to the buyers.  No scratches or dings and a great battery life too.  The item arrived with great packaging and I am impressed with this seller.Now my niece with the iPhone 17 pro max with 256 gig of storage loves her phone, she’s had it for about a month now, and yes,she paid more than me and I have a 1 terabyte storage drive on mine, and her first complaint about the iPhone 17 is, the aluminum casing gets scratched up easily forcing her to get a cover so she doesn’t have to look at the scratched up case on her new iPhone.The IPhone 16 Pro Max has a titanium frame that is solid, and I do have a case over it to protect it from drops or falls.Would I recommend this iPhone and seller on Amazon.  ABSOLUTELY YES!Alyssa

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Minor cut on the edge of camera, Side camera button not functional, poor customer service experience
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I usually don’t put feedback in reviews section, but I think this is important one and so I thought its important to provide a feedback so that customers can get a trustworthy product from Amazon renewed premium category, that really gives the customer the price point of value with money.I ordered my iPhone 16 pro max couple of days back and got it yesterday. I was very excited as I was getting 512GB storage with an amazon backed brand to claim that renewed premium category is like a new. Now as I received my phone, it all looks very nice and I start begin the setup as well as checked everything from the physical perspective if nothing is damaged, I didn’t notice anything major till my son noticed that of the lens on the back side camera have a small chip cut that can easily be observed in day light as well as buy touching it with finger. Anyway I proceed with complete setup, and begin testing the phone, everything looks to be fine, batter at 95% which is good. But then I majorly stuck on side camera button, which was not functional. I did some research on YouTube and google if some setting or config needs to change, and I followed all the steps but nothing works and the conclusion that some sensor or side button is damaged and not functioning properly and this is big red flag if I am spending close to 1000$ on renewed premium product and expecting it to at least work 4 to 5 years. I also want to mention that, amazon send me the lighting cable, instead of usb C cable.Anyway next morning I called customer care to report my feedback and explain all the details, my concern was not that I can’t return it or can’t get the refund. But my biggest concern was of Trust in the branding for renewed premium category of product. Because if Vendor is claiming what they are selling then it supposed to be that way. Because if I have to buy a renewed premium category product I may think twice or more before taking that decision, and I think used premium category is a big market, so seller should focus on quality and maintaining the brand and not to sell the defective product to customer and create so much frustration.But the good thing is at least Renewed premium category is claiming to return and refund upto 365 days that customer support specialist also told me to not worry and return and try order another one, because its rare that such kind of issue come, but anyway I see 11% of customers report bad experience so this matters.Anyway I am retuning this phone today with less than 14 hours of receiving, I am not sure if I will order again, because of all such a big hassle in the whole experience of waiting the product to arrive, setup everything, and test out and its all about experience how much you want to invest in that effort.I am updating my review on May 22 regarding my experience with customer service while following up on my refund. It has now been two days since my return.On May 20, I spoke with an Amazon specialist about a defective product and requested a replacement. I was advised that the best option would be to initiate a return and return at Whole Foods and that I would receive a refund within a week, after which I could place a new order.However, today, when I contacted customer support to check the status of my refund, I had a very disappointing experience. The representative was rude, yelled her voice, and informed me that the refund would take up to 30 days.  So be prepare, if you get a defective product then you stuck with your money and wont be able to buy another unless you get your money back. This is one of the worst experience i had as i cant use the product that i paid for, and the money also stuck for a month, that i cant use to buy another phoneShe also stated that the previous information I received about a 7-day refund was incorrect. She was not willing to listen to my concerns and ended the call abruptly.I have never encountered such poor customer service from Amazon before. This experience was frustrating and does not align with Amazon’s stated commitment to being customer-obsessed.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I ordered this phone for my elderly father. I had a lot of difficulty setting up the phone, as it arrived dead and took a long time to charge. Things seemed kind  of glitchy at first  but  I assumed  it  was  because I'm  used to iOS. I got it set up and went home (70 miles away).Two  days later  my dad  called asking for  help because the phone  was inundated  with weird pop ups (mind you, I only know what  he  was  able to articulate to me, because when you're  close  to 80 years  old, technology  is confusing). He could not answer any calls on the phone. I asked  him to wait until I could make another trip to sort the phone out.At that point, the  phone  started  overheating. Impatient, my dad  took it to a Verizon store and  they told  him that  the battery was  shot, extremely overheated. My dad  shut  the phone off  and let it sit for a while.Fast forward  to turning the phone back on and all the same issues kept happening. He couldn't make any calls from the phone and any calls that came in, the phone would not answer them. In frustration over missing calls  for two weeks  (since we activated the phone), my dad  threw it, smashed it and shattered it to smithereens. I clearly couldn't return it for replacement  at that point. Probably would have gotten more runaround and aggravation anyway.I've personally had mostly good luck with Amazon pre-owned phones. Unfortunately, this one was a complete loss. It wasn't in the condition that was advertised and showed more visible defects than described and didn't even come with a charging cable. Nothing, just a used and clearly non-functional phone in the box.Dad dug an old flip phone out of the junk drawer and he's using that now and happy as a clam...despite wasting over $200 on this phone and an additional $50 for a case and charging cables that he doesn't need now.I can't recommend the seller that sold this phone. The phone clearly hadn't been tested or inspected. If it had, they would have found the overheating issue immediately.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Time to update your old "out of update coverage" phone to an S24!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this refurb under the "excellent" listing, and it was. It came in looking like it was brand new and had never been out in the wild. There was not a scratch on it and it worked flawlessly. One of the main reasons I've stuck with Samsung over the years is that they have keep extending the amount of time that they promise to keep pushing out security updates for their phones. It's not necessary to me to have one that is cutting edge, so buying a phone that's 12 to 15 months old that I can get a steep discount on k(but still has four to five years of update coverage guaranteed) makes sense to me. I hate having to move data from one phone to another, so I can kick that can down the road for the next five or six years. The phone itself works very well, it's a lot snappier than the S10 it replaced, and the camera is excellent. I have no complaints about the phone or the process of buying a refurb and will continue to do so in the foreseeable future.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The phone was unlocked and in excellent condition. Put my T-Mobile sim card in and it worked as expected.  After 6 months T-Mobile black-listed this phone's IMEI and it couldn't get on the network. I took it to T-Mobile and they said the previous owner bought it on a payment plan and didn't make payments, and their account became delinquent, which triggers the black-listing. The renewed seller was YY Wireless. I was obviously out of my 90-day return window.  I contacted the seller and told them the situation. They said when they sold the phone, the IMEI was clear, and have no way of knowing that the previous owner is not making payments. I can understand that.  However, YY Wireless is taking the phone back and will refund me for the full purchase price.  I commend YY Wireless for doing this. So this review is not so much about the phone (good phone), but about YY Wireless.  Good on them.  I am buying another renewed phone from them.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It's NOT an AT&T device and works fine!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Those that are saying it's an AT&T locked phone is NOT correct! It is a renewed mobile phone so until you switch to the new device from your mobile carrier, it will state the previous carrier. Example, I have Metro PCS so to activate the new device, I logged into my Metro PCS account from the old device, selected 'switch to new device' then entered the new IMEI 15-digit number and wa-hoo...success! Powered off the old device, inserted the new SIM card into the new device, allowed it to update and verify my phone number and I was back in action!!!! Just Google your current carrier information to activate a new device or dial *#6# on your new device to retrieve the IMEI 15-digit number.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My phone arrived undamaged, in perfect condition!  I waited to do this review until I had it for a bit to make sure everything worked right.Well....IT'S AMAZING!!!The phone was not damaged in any way.  It looked like a brand new phone, right out of the box!  Not only that, but it functions flawlessly.  I don't use all of the features (and it has a lot of them), mostly because I don't do social media stuff, or take many pictures.  However, taking pictures is absolutely amazing!  There are sooooo many options: like filters, colors, cropping, picture size, frame size, etc.  There's just a ton of them.There is also Biometric features, which I appreciate.  I had the S9+ and the fingerprint reader was on the back.  If you use the fingerprint feature on this phone, make sure you set a passcode or pin as well.  The fingerprint reader is on the screen.  It shows as a pop-up.  Of course you have to go through the fingerprint set-up first, and can choose more than one finger/thumb.  My concern is that if the screen gets damaged where the reader is, the screen probably wouldn't be able to be able to read your print.  It does NOT have an iris scanner.This IS a 5G phone, but it can connect to 4G and other networks as well.I believe there might have been a SIM card, but I honestly don't remember.  I took the SIM from my other phone and put it in this one, so I didn't need it anyway.  I use AT&T pre-paid, and it works fine.  Right out of the box.  I don't know if it's unlocked to a variety of different network or service providers.  My service provider is AT&T, and the phone I got from this seller is also AT&T.  My recommendation to anyone considering purchasing this phone, would be to contact the seller, first and ask about supported service providers.  If you have AT&T, it's a total win!  :)This phone charges super fast, and the battery life is fabulous.  For my usage, anyway.  You absolutely have to use a fast charging cable, or you'll ruin your phone.  I believe it came with a USB cable, but I can't remember if the block was included.  Either way, if you need to get a charging block, and/or cable, MAKE SURE they're fast charging!!!  I thought the cable it came with was too short for my needs, so I bought a new one on Amazon that is specifically for the S23+...and phones like it.Another recommendation I have is to get an Otterbox.  BEFORE you start using the phone.  If you drop it, then a lot of money was spent for nothing.  The camera lenses on the back protrude.  I personally have the Otterbox Defender series, as the case itself prevents the camera lenses from touching any surface when you lay the phone down.  It's the same if you lay it face down.  The cover prevents the face from touching the surface of anything.  I would seriously consider getting a high quality case with this phone, instead of a cheap knock-off.  (Not all cases are created equal.)  The phone is constructed of metal, not plastic, so it feels very well made.  It's not a light phone, but not super heavy, either.  At least to me.The phone doesn't come in an original box.  At least mine didn't.  It came with the phone and charging cable.  I can't remember if it came with the little key that opens the SIM slot.  If it doesn't, you'll need to get one.  It also doesn't come with a manual.  Also, unless you get the S23 Ultra, there is no stylus.  If that's what you're looking for, the S23+ doesn't have that capability at all.  You aren't able to get an S Pen with it, as the S Pen wouldn't function, even if you bought one and tried.I would also like to mention that it's super easy to transfer your data and contacts (and whatever else) to the S23+.  I don't have any idea about transferring from an Apple product, though.  Samsung is my go-to for phones.As for settings, there are too many to list.  There is a specific one for the battery that I would like to mention, however.  It makes it so your phone doesn't charge over 80% when fully charged, which is important.  The phone won't overcharge that way and end up ruining your battery.As for call settings, there are a lot of those as well.  For people that are hard of hearing, there are options for that.  If, on the other hand, you'd like to protect your hearing and how loud the phone can get while listening to music or talking on it, you can limit the volume.  It has features for the blind, but I don't know what that entails.  It also has the car feature, but I don't know anything about that.  I don't drive.I hope this review was helpful.  :)

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've waited about four months to post a review, giving me plenty of time to experience the phone. Let me start off by saying I spent HOURS going through different websites and sellers, trying to filter through reviews and the experience of others because... let's be real, who wants to sploof a $350+ purchase? Brand new, I would have never dropped the retail price on this phone. I did extensive delving into the sellers that offered this specific phone, and I ended up going with Soonersoft.I was hesitant, even though it says unlocked, because there are thousands of reviews out there of people having to try to refund their renewed/refurbished purchases because it's not TRULY unlocked. So I messaged the seller and asked for verification that the phone would work with my carrier ( Verizon). They quickly responded, and verified that it was actually a Verizon unlocked phone. Perfect! I put my order in and received my phone a couple of days later. It arrived in a box very much like a brand new phone would. This phone was SPOTLESS. Not a single scratch anywhere on the surface and no discoloration. I had a hiccup during setup where I didn't think it was going to work, but I waited until ALL, and I must stress ALL, of my information was synced and everything was done updating. I used my old SIM card, though this phone offers eSIM, and was able to get it working properly without needing either the seller support ( they included a card with the packaging for such cases ), or Verizon. I've had no wifi or bluetooth connectivity issues, and the fingerprint reader works flawlessly. The camera is a huge step up from my previous 5 year old phone, and the UI is intuitive as I've only ever had Samsung.Literally my ONLY gripe about this phone is actually the Verizon app itself. It'll glitch to the point I often have to completely close and reopen it several times if I want to check my data usage or pay the bill manually. I've uninstalled  and reinstalled it, cleared cache and data, and the issue persists. HOWEVER, this is not really a big issue for me personally. I can easily open my account via a chrome tab and work with my info that way.TLDR; Was very skeptical ordering a phone online, did tons of research and found the seller SoonerSoft. Shot them a compatibility question and ordered the phone. Phone was in like new condition and I had no issues after having ALL of my data transferred over. It's been running near flawlessly ( save for my carrier app ) for the past 4 months. I can solidly recommend this seller for renewed electronics. They're also very responsive to questions if you want to verify what carrier it's unlocked from.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very good value. Refurb iPhone 15 Pro, 512gb.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is the first time I've purchased an iPhone in refurb condition. However, I have had good experiences with Amazon resale/refurb products. I have to admit to being a bit hesitant and concerned about the actual quality of the phone, especially the state of the battery.Perhaps the fact that the phone arrived a few days before the expected delivery date range was a good omen. I specifically chose Amazon as the shipper/seller of the item. I felt that if there was any problems, having Amazon as the seller would entail less hassles with the resolution process.  Fortunately, there were no major issues with iPhone. The front screen was scratch-free. There was some odd substance on the titanium sides (it seemed to be glue/adhesive residue). In general, the appearance was very good/excellent.The screen does not seem to retain much of the oil/fingerprint resistance feature. But, considering it was manufactured in 2024, this reduced aspect is to be expected. I think I'll eventually add a screen protector to deal with easy cleaning and additional protection of the screen.I ran apple diagnostics, and it passed on all the tests, indicating apple parts and functions. And, while the promise is for battery over 80% (I ordered the 'Renewed-Excellent'), it actually rated at 90%, with 591 cycles. I consider it a win.After transferring from my older iPhone, I only had to redo login/password for a few apps (financial and health apps, which makes sense that they're more secure). And, it was easy to transfer the esim to the 15Pro, too.Ordered a case today, which should arrive tomorrow. I'll be researching and ordering a screen protector this weekend.Considering an Apple Certified Refurb of same model and storage would be close to $1000, this was a very good value. My thinking was the battery state was probably the vulnerable aspect. So, even if I had to replace the battery after the 90 day warranty, the $100 cost was still be a financial win. (Hopefully, the battery lives as long as my iPhone XR did, haha).Anyway, I feel I made a wise choice getting this 'Renewed-Excellent' iPhone 15 Pro/512gb via Amazon (I did research other refurb venues, btw). Picking Amazon as shipper/seller was the safe, smart move too, imho.  I would only be happier if the batty capacity was 100% and it came with a screen protector.I rate the product and experience 4.75 - 5 stars, with a very high level recommendation.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: If at first you get a defective phone, try again if you have the patience.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My phone rated Excellent Premium was defective in a way any technician would have identified  had it really been tested and reviewed before publishing the phone on Amazon's website.  Amazon give the impression that the customer should feel some comfort because of it's rating and because they are Amazon.  That doesn't work that way.  When you contact Amazon they ask about the problem and then pass on to the seller a very abridged summary.  They assure you they will help.  But all the conversation between you and Amazon disappears.  If you want to preserve this conversation and refer back, or follow up, it is nowhere to be found.  They claim to have a buyer/seller message board, but Amazon is invisible and you can't ask for more help.It turns out that part of my biggest problem was how to discover why the phone did not work. I didn't know that an Excellent premium phone can be tested and verified without the updated IOS version being downloaded and installed, and it can't.  But no where are you told that.  I spent hours on the phone with the carrier and texting with AI because I couldn't even get Apple to acknowledge my Apple account.  Then after all my efforts I was locked out for 2 hours!  It seems to me this is vital info for a new buyer like me, and it should be included by Amazon in their description.As it turned out the "board" connecting the eSim that issues the signal for cellular to work was defective.  But no experts that I consulted realized that a simple test of the eSim is to try to read a Qr code, without a functioning eSim that will not be possible and certainly that is a simple test for verifying a several hundred dollar phone before giving it an Excellent premium rating in Amazon. For several other reasons too lengthy for this review, I now believe Amazon's rating of refurbished phones is BS.  And their help is minuscule.  Despite that, I ordered a replacement iPhone 15 pro through Amazon, again got suckered in on a non updated IOS, but so far, now that my Apple a/c is recognized, the phone appears to be truly excellent.  I knew enough to avoid the extra cost of PREMIUM.Update, I'm still waiting for my refund on the first phone 19 days after paying for it.I've updated my review from one to 3 stars because the replacement phone is in excellent condition as rated, and much more deserving of a Premium designation, which the seller did not claim.  I remain disappointed in the Amazon role in the transaction but they do have a large inventory to choose from.  Why can't Amazon include in it's sale promotion description a warning to be sure to check whether the phone has the latest IOS upgrade, don't trust the seller.  Not knowing to do this cost meat at least half a day all told.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Powerful iPhone with a Premium Design
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Apple iPhone 15 Pro Max is a great option for anyone looking for a high-end smartphone without necessarily paying full price for a brand-new model. The Black Titanium finish looks sleek and premium, and the overall design feels modern and durable.The 6.7-inch display is one of the standout features. The screen is bright, sharp, and great for watching videos, browsing the internet, taking photos, and using apps. The ProMotion display also makes scrolling and animations feel smooth and responsive.The camera system is another major highlight. The different camera options make it easy to take detailed photos in a variety of situations, while the video quality is excellent for recording everyday moments. The 5x telephoto camera is especially useful when you want to capture subjects from farther away.The performance is very fast thanks to the A17 Pro chip. Apps open quickly, multitasking feels smooth, and the phone handles demanding games and other tasks well. The 256GB of storage also provides plenty of room for photos, videos, apps, and other files.Since this is a renewed device, the condition can depend on the individual unit, so it is important to check the seller's description and renewal warranty before purchasing. Being unlocked is a major advantage because it gives you more flexibility when choosing a compatible carrier.The battery life is also good for everyday use, although actual battery performance on a renewed phone can vary depending on its battery health and previous use.Overall, the iPhone 15 Pro Max 256GB in Black Titanium is a powerful and premium phone with an excellent display, strong cameras, fast performance, and plenty of storage. For someone who wants a Pro Max experience at a potentially lower price through a renewed model, this is a solid option.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: BE AWARE OF THE RISKS - I spent hours fixing Amazons issueBE AWARE OF THE RISKS - I spent hours fixing Amazons issue
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Updated: since writing the below review, I have received my second 15 pro max renewed premium, set it up, and handled the refund from the first one. Amazon customer support also offered me a generous discount on the new phone for all the hassle (which I somewhat needed to initiate asking for, I doubt they would have offered that to begin with). If I had to do it all over again - I would have still gone this route since apple refurbished hasn’t released this model yet, but moving forward- I will probably order straight from apple refurbished next time or just get a new iPhone. When factoring the discount I got on this one that’s one year old, I paid about 2/3 the cost for this compared to the latest model, so I can’t complain. All that said, in general I am one who much more values my time and ease over saving a quick bucks. Especially if that quick buck saved costs me HOURS of my life in hassle. If you’re like me in that sense - proceed with caution. I trust Amazon will help make it right if you don’t get a great phone as expected, but even if that’s the case, you’re probably in for quite the hoops to jump through in order to make that happen.Here’s my original, unedited review:I ordered the iPhone 15 Pro Max refurbished and it arrived last night. After spending a good 3+ hours setting it up, I realized the lens for the main camera was broken. From the outside, you can’t see any issue. It wasn’t until I opened up the camera app that I actually saw it didn’t work.“Renewed Premium” carries a certain standard with it, and this certainly does not meet that in the slightest. On top of that, upon calling customer support, I was told that I would not be able to do anything unless I deactivated the phone and remove my Apple ID from it. Wouldn’t have been the end of the world if I needed to go back to my other phone for a bit, however, in order to set up this phone with the eSIM, deactivated my previous SIM card. Upon explaining all of that to customer support, I was told there was nothing they could do unless I deactivated this phone (leaving me without a phone until they received this and shipped me a new one)I was then told to call Apple to see what they can do, when honestly, this is their mistake. Either way, I called apple and it was going to be another set of hoops to jump through with scheduling appointments and all that. Plus since I didn’t have apple care, if they needed to repair the camera, I would still be without a phone. So even if Apple was able to help fix this, the issue of me not having a phone would still be there. Had I broken this camera myself - I would certainly except those terms given there’s not much else I could do. However, this was given to me in this condition and for Amazon to leave me with the responsibility of fixing their mistake due to carelessness in inspection and quality control is absurd.So whether I like it or not, I am now STUCK with the responsibility of cleaning this up since my account is connected to this phone now. What at one point could have been a great gift to myself has turned into the biggest hassle I’ve experienced buying/returning anything, probably ever.I’m going to give this one more shot as I’ve now ordered another iPhone from them to be delivered shortly, however, it’s also required me to spend another ~$1000 in having that iPhone sent prior to me getting my refund. This is absolutely ridiculous and unacceptable. Even if this next phone is perfect, I’m likely never going to order from the Amazon refurbished store again. I’ll either go straight to Apple refurbished, or brand new, for any of my future phone/laptop/device purchases.On top of all this hassle, I’ll certainly have to spend another few hours setting up my replacement phone once it arrives.All the time I’ve invested into this so far has NOT been even close worth the “nice discount” on a premium refurbished phone that should have arrived without issue to begin with.Amazon - take note. Change your policies. Making this the customer’s mess to clean up is not acceptable.Potential buyers - BEWARE of the risks.I’ll plan to update this review if anything changes. But like I said, even if the next phone I ordered is perfect, I still give this a 1-star review for all the hassle and lack of responsibility the company took to resolve this.P.s. i’ll also add that I am a quite understanding and peaceful person. The person I spoke with from customer support was doing his absolute best to help me, but this was clearly a bigger issue than he had the power to solve. I requested to have this escalated to upper management and was told the same thing. Whoever is the one making decisions about what can and can’t be done needs to hear about this.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Apple iPhone 11 Review: A Reliable Backup That Feels Like New
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Update:  I'm back with an update on our journey with the iPhone 11, and let me tell you, it's been quite the rollercoaster. Initially, I bought one for my daughter from a different seller, and it was, to put it mildly, a bit of a disaster. We had issues left and right – Face ID not working, the phone overheating – you name it. So, we returned it, feeling a bit skeptical about the whole refurbished scene.But here's where the plot twists: we decided to give it another go, this time purchasing from the Amazon resellers store, specifically from a shop called Hybrid IT. And oh boy, what a difference! The iPhone we received this time around was nothing short of impeccable. It arrived with all the essentials – a charger, a charging cable, and even a SIM card tool, all neatly packed. The phone itself? It could've fooled me for brand new.This experience really hammered home the lesson that when it comes to refurbished goods, the "who" is just as crucial as the "what." The quality and condition of the product can vary wildly depending on the seller. Hybrid IT sent out an excellent product that exceeded our expectations in every way.For those of you wary about diving into the world of refurbished electronics, let this be a testament. With the right seller, you can get your hands on a device that feels brand new, without the hefty price tag. We're over the moon with our iPhone 11, and I'll be sure to keep you all posted if anything changes. But for now, it seems like we've struck gold.--------------------I recently found myself in need of a quick replacement after my daughter accidentally broke her phone. The Apple iPhone 11, 64GB in black, seemed like a promising choice, primarily because we needed something that could be set up swiftly and would perform seamlessly as a backup.Out of the box, the iPhone 11 felt like a brand-new device despite being a model released a few years back. The sleek black finish and the familiar design immediately caught my eye, reassuring me that this choice would not disappoint.Setting up the iPhone 11 was mostly straightforward, especially with the unlocked version making it easy to switch from the old device. The transfer of data and settings from the previous iPhone was seamless, thanks to Apple's ecosystem. However, we hit a slight snag with the Face ID setup - it took a bit longer than expected to get it working properly. Despite this hiccup, once configured, Face ID has been working flawlessly.The iPhone 11's performance has been impressive. The touch screen is responsive, making navigation and typing a breeze. Wi-Fi connectivity is fast, ensuring that browsing and app downloads are efficient. Although it's not the latest model, it handles everyday tasks with ease, from streaming video content to gaming, without any noticeable lag.The main issue we encountered was the initial difficulty in setting up Face ID. It required a few attempts to configure, which was a minor inconvenience in an otherwise smooth setup process. After overcoming this challenge, the phone has been working perfectly.Overall, this refurbished Apple iPhone 11 has proven to be a reliable and efficient backup phone. Its ease of setup, fast Wi-Fi, and responsive touch screen make it feel like a new device. The hiccup with Face ID setup was a small obstacle that, once overcome, didn't detract from the overall positive experience. I would recommend the iPhone 11 to anyone in need of a quick replacement or a dependable backup device

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: iPhone 13 mini is everything I ever wanted.iPhone 13 mini is everything I ever wanted.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’m writing this review with a few caveats I will get to. First of all, the iPhone 13 mini is truly the best iPhone for people who want a phone that feels like a phone and not like they are carrying around a tablet. I have been using the iPhone 16 Pro since it came out and had no idea what I was missing in this older model until I was talking to a friend about his. He told me it was the best phone ever made and he would not get rid of his until he couldn’t get replacement parts or unless they made a new updated mini, which it sounds like they have no plans to do (a shame). I was telling him that I have been traveling with work and when I’m pulling a bag, I need to be able to work my phone well with one hand. The 16 Pro is not good for this. I don’t like cases, I don’t want to use a pop socket - I just want a pretty sleek unencumbered iPhone. So I was on a mission and it’s not an easy one when you’re picky about the condition and the phone can only be found in the used/renewed/refurbished channels. I had hesitations about buying from Amazon resale because of other items I’ve gotten from them that didn’t seem like they were inspected. I took a risk. I purchased the starlight 256gb from Amazon (not a marketplace seller). It was still a pretty penny considering the age of the mini, but the minis hold their value due to the cult following they have. I received it and it was absolutely perfect - didn’t look like it had ever been used, though the battery capacity was 85%…which was okay but nothing wonderful. In the meantime, I decided I would prefer the 512gb since I plan to keep this a long time, so I decided to order one, also from Amazon resale, since the 256 was in such pristine condition and I knew I had 90 days to decide regardless. The 512gb through Amazon was a crazy price…marked as excellent but over $550 with taxes (I had paid $330 for the 256gb). Cut to a day later, I see that a seller has the 512 starlight marked as excellent and it was $385. I reached out to them and asked them about the battery health and they were wonderful - got back to me really quickly and said 99%. So I thought, well, for $385 vs $550, I’ll cancel the Amazon order and order this one. Unfortunately it was too late to cancel the Amazon one - it had already shipped - so my intention was to just send it straight back as soon as it was delivered. The one from the actual cellphone reseller got here quickly and for the price, was represented well - it did have 2 corners with blemishes that look like they’re from a drop, but they weren’t terrible but having seen the pristine 256gb version from Amazon, I was being overly picky. The battery was 100%, as they had told me, which was great, but what I noticed was the screen had been replaced. I’m okay with screen replacements - any phone from 2021 has probably had one, as well as any battery that shows 100% on a phone from 2021 is a replaced battery. These are not bad things. What I do know from having a screen replaced years ago through one of the shops that uses an aftermarket part is the screens are not as flat as apple’s genuine screen if you get a replacement from them. It almost has waves in it, especially along the edges. They look fine if you aren’t picky to the degree I am, or looking at the phone from an angle, but I’ve found they are not always reliable screens with regard to the responsiveness. As soon as I saw this, I packed it back up and set up a return through the seller and took it straight to the UPS store. Cut to my next Amazon delivery, the 512gb model that I had been unable to cancel arrives. Since the one from the reseller didn’t work out for me, I said, well, let’s check this out because if it’s perfect, then I guess it’s worth the $550 spent. Open it up and WOW! The body of it is just like the 256 I had gotten. Pristine - not a drop ding or scratch in sight. Perfect screen…remarkable…but I wanted to check the battery. When I got it up and running, I checked the battery capacity and it was at 100%. Under the battery details it even lists it as a Genuine battery, so it was “renewed” with Apple OEM. I could not be more thrilled even though it cost way more than a phone from 2021 should. But I’m keeping it for the long haul so it’s worth it knowing I don’t have a battery replacement in the near future. I’ve got the 90 days to see how it functions but I feel pretty good about this one.TL;DR - the iPhone mini is a phone you will be addicted to after use. It’s so functional and what a “phone” should be. Do not hesitate to order one shipped from and sold by Amazon.com. I can confirm they have fantastic quality control when it comes to their phones. If you pick a reseller other than Amazon, just make sure you get the 90 day return and that there aren’t “restocking” fees buried in their policies.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Pleasantly surprised. Excellent condition, no scratches or dings, passed two diagnostics..
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was on a waiting list for a 'Renewed Premium'. Seemed to be a long waiting list. I finally gave up and went with a 'Renewed' advertised in excellent condition. Given Amazon's generous return policy, returning it would have been painless if there had been issues. I probably wouldn't have tried this with an online retailer other than Amazon and Apple.The supplier was TECHMINT, Amazon the purchase portal. There seems to be a number of 'Amazon-qualified suppliers' involved. To know who you're buying from, the 'ships from/sold by' info. is on the right side of the product page. There may also be differences in packaging and accessories. Best to read through the advertising to know exactly what you're buying. Or contact the supplier before purchasing. Given that Amazon backs these purchases, not a concern.It arrived without scratches, dings, or apparent wear. Looks like new. That said, those buying a 'Renewed' phone should expect varying degrees of condition within the parameters of Amazon's advertising. I'd suggest buying a 'Renewed Premium' for your best chance of a like-new phone. I probably got lucky with a 'Renewed'.It shipped in a *very* well designed and protective box designed for phones. Not much larger than the boxes Apple packages iPhones in and similarly sturdy. Well suited for protecting the phone during shipping. If you plan on shipping your phone or storing a back-up, I'd suggest keeping it. The box has spacers to accommodate different sizes. Kudos to the packaging engineers. Well done.It was delivered with 100% battery health which almost certainly means that the phone was opened up and the battery replaced. The likelihood of a 'renewed' 13 Mini arriving with battery health at 100% is slim to none. I assume that they did this because the phone was traded in with < 80% battery health. Amazon advertising states that the phone will arrive with battery health of ≥ 80%. Notably, the battery was recognized by iOS as 'genuine' (thanks TECHMINT). Batteries that are not can lead to various issues, most importantly, safety issues. Look up "how to check if an iPhone battery is genuine". If it isn't, I'd suggest returning it to the supplier.Side note about iPhone battery replacement: If/when you have an iPhone battery replaced, I'd highly recommend scheduling it through Apple. Apple often contracts with third parties to do this in addition to Apple stores. When third parties sign up for this, they're held to a high standard and you're guaranteed to receive a 'genuine' battery. More importantly, if there's a problem you'll have the full weight of Apple behind you to resolve any issues.I'd also suggest reaching out to the supplier before purchase and asking what the battery health will be. In my experience with the iPhone 12 Mini, once you drop into the high 80% range, battery life becomes more noticeable. Note that Apple recommends replacing an iPhone battery when it reaches 80% battery health.I ran two diagnostics to check functions. In both cases, no issues. One of the diagnostics is built into iOS. You'll need iOS 17 or later and not a beta release. Search for 'built in iPhone diagnostic' for instructions. There's another which makes doing this quite a bit easier. From the Apple app store search for 'Phone Doctor Plus'. It's not a diagnostic as much as it's a function check but good for making sure everything works. There's a free and paid version. There are others but these are the only two I've tried.The advertising stated that an MFi certified charging/data cable ships with the phone. Mine shipped with a 3ft braided USB C to Lightning charging cable. No branding or print on the cable, no included documentation, no packaging. It appears similar to what you'll sometimes see without packaging and hanging from peg racks in convenience stores.I have no reason to believe that the provided cable isn't MFi certified and from a reliable manufacturer but without more information, best to use an Apple product or something from an established aftermarket supplier such as Belkin or Anker. Look for 'MFi certified' especially if you want fast charging capability. There are reasons USB C cables can be pricey, especially those designed for high power delivery.Mine shipped without a charger. I'd say the same about a charger as I did about the cable - MFi certified and from a reputable manufacturer - Apple, Belkin, Anker, etc. For the 13 Mini, Apple recommends a minimum of a 20 watt charger for optimal/fast charging . Apple's is about 20 dollars. It's also what Apple recommends for powering *the original* MagSafe accessory. The updated version of the MagSafe charger supports faster charging and according to Apple, a minimum of a 30 watt charger for optimal performance.Some suppliers advertise that a sim card removal tool is included. Mine didn't. If yours shipped with a sim card (mine did not), I'd suggest reading through the pros and cons of SIM vs eSIM. If eSIM meets your needs, I'd recommend removing the SIM and switching to eSIM. Switching to eSIM can be done in your phone's settings. No expertise or hardware required. Although unlikely if buying from an 'Amazon-qualified supplier' (I assume), SIM cards can be compromised. If you need a SIM card, best to get one from your carrier instead of a mystery SIM.The Apple leather case has been my go-to for the last 2-3 iPhones. Very well designed, doesn't add significant bulk, comfortable to grip,  no sharp edges and it slips into and out of a pocket easily. The drop protection has proven to be excellent. Great case for all but extreme circumstances. They're relatively pricey so If you're looking to save, there are often Amazon customer returns available. eBay is another good source.The iPhone 12 mini and 13 mini cases are not interchangeable. I tried. The camera lens housings are different. The 12 mini case will not fit the 13 mini. The 13 mini case will fit the 12 mini but there will be a gap on the right side of the lens housing.Not to overstate it but If you're considering both the 12 mini and 13 mini, battery life may be problematic for heavy users. If you have a full size phone with a larger battery at ≥ 90% battery health (guesstimate) and often find yourself scrambling to find a charger, the Mini may not be for you.If you're on the move a lot without convenient charging options, a small power bank (≤ 5000mAh) will bring some peace of mind and a lot of convenience. Great when traveling. Definitely stick with time tested manufacturers. Anker and Belkin sell a wide variety. Note that the TSA only allows powerbanks in carry-ons.Apple discontinued it's iPhone power banks (Magsafe Battery Pack). As of this writing, you can still find them new from third party sources such as Walmart and eBay. Never buy used. There are confirmed and very convincing counterfeits out there so I'd be cautious about which supplier you choose. Look up "how to check if an Apple Magsafe Battery Pack is counterfeit".*Update* Apple reintroduced it's magsafe battery pack now called the iPhone Air MagSafe Battery. It was designed specifically for the iPhone Air and reportedly works with other iPhones - sort of. Not recommended. Fit issues.If you're looking at both the 12 and 13 Minis, the 13 Mini uses an A15 processor which is somewhat more energy efficient and slightly faster. It also has a ~10% larger battery. There are quite a few other differences including an upgraded camera.In day to day use, I found the differences to be negligible. I suspect that most people wouldn't be able to tell the difference without knowing what to look for.Definitely worth reading comparison reviews. Some of the updates will be important for some, less so for others. Search for "iPhone 13 mini vs iPhone 12 mini". If you read only one, Laptopmag.com published a well grounded, real-world comparison, no hype.Long term, the 13 Mini will receive system/feature updates from Apple for about a year longer. This may be the most value added difference. Generally speaking, Apple devices continue to receive security updates beyond the point that they are no longer supported with system/feature updates. Current estimates seem to be late 2027 for system/feature updates and 2030/2031 for security updates. When the security updates stop, best to replace the phone.If Apple's AI (Apple Intelligence) is a feature you want, it isn't supported in the Mini's. You can still use cloud based AI services but without the privacy and security features Apple bakes into it's AI. You'll need a minimum of an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max to use Apple's AI.Happy customer. I'm fully committed to the Mini form factor/dimensions. I carry it all day in a front or back pocket and barely know it's there. Having a phone with more screen, battery and features is nice but after the novelty wears off, having a phone that disappears into a pocket is more important for some of us. Sadly, not enough of us for Apple to justify continued production. When I need to replace it, perhaps Mini's will be back in the menu from Apple. Hope so.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Amazon Refurbished Excellent: What a Joke!Amazon Refurbished Excellent: What a Joke!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: After much research, I decided to choose Amazon's refurbished program over Apple, Best Buy, or Walmart. I've had much success with Walmart's refurbished products, but selected this phone based on the fact it was the highest level for Amazon - "Refurbished Excellent". I should've returned it as soon as I opened it, and found the back cover was not original. The phone did check out as actual Apple iPhone, so I bought the highest quality case - an Otterbox (commuter series) - and started using it. I don't even know how I got the first two cracks on the screen (chose iPhone over other brands because the screen is supposedly so much sturdier), but the final blow followed shortly. The shattered spot happened when it fell out from under my arm, landing on the side of the case. I went to the local Batteries Plus to ask a price for screen replacement; the employee took the protective case off to take a look, and we discovered the rear phone cover was shattered! Fast forward about a month, now the battery is failing. One minute it will show 90%, then all of a sudden it shuts down, restarts, and shows 10%. My phone is essential for so many reasons - work, communication with aged parents on-call emergencies, and so much more. Amazon should be ashamed of calling a product "Refurbished Excellent", when it falls apart after only a few months of use! Over $400, and now it will take more than that to repair! Extremely dissatisfied.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Amazon came through with an almost perfect i13 Pro 1TB
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: A bit of a story here... last year I bought a refurb'ed, like new iPhone 13 from Amazon... and returned it (and bought one elsewhere, that was much nicer, and less money).This year - being entirely comfortable with the i13 level specs - I decided to upgrade to an i13 Pro... and - because of last year's experience - went elsewhere first. What I got from them this time was definitely not what I ordered (it was supposed to be "pristine"... what I got was scratched up junk).So I came back to Amazon, and ordered the only "used-like new" offering on the i13 Pro "list" that day.What I got, well, wasn't (i.e., wasn't "used-like new"). Again. Sigh. (I have a ton of experience with buying "used-like new" stuff from Amazon over the years, and I know what to expect... and this wasn't it.)But.What I received was a "refurbished-excellent" i13 Pro (the same category as the i13 I ordered last year... which was again, anything but, back then, lol). The category which is is now listed on the order form.(Why would they change the category? When it wasn't what I ordered? -Dunno.)HOWEVER.... big "however".It was... almost... perfect: a few tiny scratches around the lightning port is all a minute examination found wrong (the previous owner had mostly used mag-charging I imagine).And... the battery health - while entirely within the spec for Amazon refurbished (i.e., "80% or greater") - was still a disappointment at only 84%.Still. Cosmetic-wise... acceptable. More than acceptable, even. Agreeably nice... obviously: as I kept it. (Note: I wouldn't review it if I hadn't kept it.)Note: For long term use of any iPhone, to avoid battery related issues, Apple recommends replacing the battery when its below 80% battery health... which repair cost from Apple is about $90 or so... iow, not a big deal. Look, I'm not the target demographic for a new Apple phone anyways; especially their Pro. So sending the phone in for a new battery, especially for what I paid for the 1TB version, is a-okay. And figured into the price.But - other than battery health... and those few tiny [mostly unnoticeable] scratches - I paid quite a bit less (saved a couple of hundred over the "other guys" offerings) at Amazon for a truly ultra-clean i13 Pro - with 1TB capacity - which is in otherwise almost perfect condition.And while its minor flaws render it most certainly NOT in the "used-like new" category... the savings over market costs for a 1TB version rendered my objections to the category moot: it was more than good enough as "refurbished-like new" lol.While YMMV, well... after all... in the final analysis... this one is a keeper.Thanks Amazon.Just keep in mind: all refurb's are "luck of the draw". Amazon is great about their return policy. Take a chance. You'll save money... maybe a bunch of money.Final word: recommend.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This was my first purchase of a "premium renewed" smartphone. The Amazon description says "Tested for battery health and guaranteed to come with a battery that exceeds 90% of original capacity." On the iPhone Pro 13 I received, the battery was 90 percent — it didn't "exceed" that number. Ultimately I returned this phone for two reasons: First the pictures look over-sharpened in some instances and almost like a painting in others. Having come from a much older phone that did not over-process the images, I was shocked to see that the HDR was so aggressive.  I thought I had nowhere to go but up after such a long time between upgrades, only to learn this has apparently been a trend in iPhone cameras in recent years. The only way I was going to obtain the menu option to turn off HDR was to drop back to an 11 or 12, so I bought the 12 Pro instead, which unlike this phone — which took a week to arrive — shipped in one day. I am happier with the fact that the Pro 12 is lighter weight and slimmer, with a better sense of balance thanks to the fact that the camera bumps are smaller.The iPhone Pro 13 features the older emergency SOS function but it is only as good as one's cell tower connectivity, whereas the 14 and newer also have SOS and roadside assistance functionality via satellite. Based on where I live (mountains, bad cell coverage) I was torn between this purchase and the iPhone 14 Pro series, especially after I realized that a third party seller here on Amazon was offering a "excellent condition" renewed model for what I paid for this older model. Having said this, the iPhone Pro 14 has had reports of overheating and/or lackluster battery performance compared to the iPhone 13 Pro. I also like the fact that the iPhone 13 Pro does NOT have the "always on" screen common to newer Pro models. Another notable difference is that the iPhone 13 Pro (and earlier) have a physical SIM tray whereas the newer 15 Pros are eSIMs. Finally, the iPhone Pro 13 and earlier uses a lightening cord vs. USB-C on current-generation iPhones. (I'm not interested in using a different charging cord/setup than my spouse, especially while traveling.)The VerdictI very much appreciate the excellent cosmetic appearance — there were no scratches or gouges to be found anywhere on the phone I received — but keeping the Pro 13 was not an option. In a video I took of a flock of birds flying just after the sun set behind a hillside, I could make out a round dust spot visible against the cloudless, pale gold sky — dead center in the bottom of the frame (landscape mode). Honestly, I probably never would have seen it in broad daylight because the HDR takes the blue sky and darkens it down so much the dust spot would have been masked — but the light I was shooting against at dusk was just a tad bit paler than the dust spot, allowing me to appreciate that the lenses were not in the perfect shape they initially appeared. Upon further inspection, using a flashlight, I noted some kind of residue *behind* two out of the three lenses. (Supposedly these lenses are sealed but per the reviews here mine is not the first report of dust spots in photos.)Overall, I don't feel like I received the "premium renewed" experience, in part because the shipping was slow (nearly four days before Amazon assigned tracking) and battery health was less than expected (others here reported at or near 100%!). Ultimately, I returned the Pro 13 and bought an iPhone Pro 12 from another seller. Not only did I pay less and end up with a slimmer, lightweight phone that feels better in the hand, but I actually like the camera quality better because it is among a very small number of iPhones where it is actually possible to turn off the HDR.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Alright so I have had this phone since around the second week of December. Everything functions perfectly, no marks or scratches, the phone was in perfect condition and my battery is also very good and usually lasts the whole day and is in around 20 percent once I get home and I use my phone alot when at work and school so take that how you want to. However some problems did occur as when I tried to put a phone service on this phone it kept getting prompted to contact T-Mobile to set up e-sim and T-Mobile was not at all helpful and hanged up multiple times after putting me on hold for an hour. How ever I was able to work around this by scanning the QR code given to me by my phone provider instead to set up a e-sim. One last thing you might want to be informed of is that the camera on the back is very good but the front camera is good but you usually have to have ideal lighting as even in night vision when it seems to be a little dark where you are the camera is blurry. All that being said I recommend this phone to any one looking for a flagship level phone for a low price but be aware of the e-sim having to be worked around.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I purchased this phone because I wanted to try out GrapheneOS. The phone works, and I've decided I really like GrapheneOS. So over all, it has served it's purpose.My biggest complaint is that it overheats during zoom meetings. I don't know why it does this, but it makes it difficult to be on a zoom call for more than 10 minutes even with the case removed and the charging cord unplugged.My next complaint is that the usbc port is starting to have connection issue and it's been less than a year. That's probably my fault because it seems to happen to all my phones regardless of brand.My last complaint is that it doesn't have an sd card slot. The fastest most straightforward way to transfer gigabytes of storage from one phone to another is to swap the sd card, but that's not an option with this phone. I know you can put an sd card in a usb stick and plug it into the usbc port, but that seems to have slower transfer speed and be vulnerable to being bumped or unplugged in the middle of a transfer.Things I like about this phone include:-Good battery life (GraphenOS helps with that by limiting bloat wear and data collection from running in the background)-The fingerprint sensors makes login quick and easy-It has options for both physical sim and e-simsPeople also say that pixel phones have good cameras. I'm not enough of a photographer to really know the difference, but I haven't had any issues with the camera.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First off, I never write reviews, but after my recent experiences I thought this might help some others.Needed to replace an aging IPhone which was still working great, but a lot of apps needing newer IOS.  So, not looking for the lastest/greatest, just a good update.  Decided IPh 14+ was a good option.Here were my first 3 strikes :1) I purchased an “Excellent” OPEN BOX phone from Best Buy.  It came in a box sealed with Geek Squad tape.  When opened, the phone had tons of fingerprints all over it, front and back; not a great first impression.  After going through the startup process I was greeted with a screen that informed me that the phone had remote management software installed on it.  Basically unusable.2) I returned it and they replaced it with another “Excellent” OPEN BOX.  Same thing – both phones had been previously owned by some company (now out of business) who had loaded remote management software on the phones. So… these are expensive, unusable bricks, and shame on BB/Geek Squad for selling these phones to the public.3) After that experience I decided to give Amazon a try and bought a phone supplied by WOOT, as I have had good experiences with other Woot purchases.  The phone arrived in a beat up generic box with the inside packaging worse than the outside.  On the positive side, the phone was cosmetically very good with no obvious scratches, etc.  So, everything looked good until I checked the battery health.  81%.  NOT GOOD. Yes, it meets the described spec of >80% for their “Excellent” condition, but will going to be into the Apple service condition in a couple of weeks.  Returned to Amazon/Woot and waiting for refund.After reading a ton of reviews I decided to give it one more shot and get a “Premium” condition directly from Amazon.com. Most of the reviews of these phones were much better than all of the other vendors.  They are definitely more expensive but come with a 365 day warranty vs 90 day and spec at >90% battery life. Phone arrived today. It was VERY nicely packaged in a SEALED shrink wrapped professional looking box. Opened the box and found a phone with what appeared to be the original Apple protective film still in place on the front and back.  Battery was dead so after a quick charge I was able to check battery health…… 100% and 0 charge cycles.  Basically this is a brand NEW, NEVER USED phone.I can’t say how impressed I was after three bad experiences.  I saved a couple $hundred compared to BB or Apple and got a brand new phone …..  It’s all about the journey  !!!
